summary: Cold read of the ask-period-control plan draft. Seven findings accepted, one rejected. The sharpest was structural: C4 ordered scope before mapping before periods, but the resolver reaches its mapping lookup only when a period is already supplied, so as written 'no mapping' and 'no periods loaded' could not be told apart - the plan now names the period-free lookup that ordering requires. C3 was proving a SERVER claim from a frontend task. Replace-in-place assumed per-turn state that use-ask.ts does not have. The live check would have run against the mock provider, which always clarifies, and could have reported green having proved nothing. The rejected finding claimed chat.service.ts needs D-0006 treatment; it is not in .prettierignore - the real exposure is chat.constants.ts.
gaps: C4's ordering had no resolution seam: SelectionResolverService.resolve() reaches its mapping lookup only when a period is supplied and throws SelectionPeriodUnavailableError before it can report anything else, so 'no mapping' and 'no periods loaded' were indistinguishable as written.
C4 contradicted itself: it listed 'no period options' as part of the BlockedByPolicy scope outcome while separately requiring 'no periods loaded' to be its own NotSupported case.
C3 was assigned to the wrong task: zero-selector-calls is a server claim provable only by a ChatService test over a fake LlmProvider, and a frontend task can prove only that it posted the selection.

Replace-in-place had no state model: use-ask.ts holds ONE global isPending and ONE global error and only appends, so a failed rerun would either blank the answer or surface its failure away from the turn it belongs to.

Surface Impact was a path list rather than the classified rows the planner contract requires - runtime behavior, API, data/schema, CLI/ops, UI, docs, tests - with a reason on every Deferred and Unchanged-by-design row.

The live functional check named only WAREHOUSE_PG_*, but the default provider is mock and MockLlmProvider ALWAYS returns clarify, so the check could appear to pass the clarification criteria while proving nothing.

The two new response fields were not reconciled against decisions 0012/0019: /api/chat documents its request body and error statuses but its 201 carries only a description, with no typed response DTO.
contradictions: The cold read asserted that changing chat.service.ts requires D-0006 treatment of .prettierignore and tools/quality-gate.test.mjs. REJECTED on inspection: chat.service.ts is NOT in .prettierignore, nor are contract/src/api.ts, ask-panel.tsx or use-ask.ts. The D-0006 exposure is real but sits on a file the read did not name - backend/src/chat/chat.constants.ts, which IS listed and is where the new failure messages belong.
resolutions: C4 now names the missing seam explicitly: SelectionResolverService gains a period-free mapping lookup over the same master data resolve() already uses, and chat.service.ts calls it before consulting periods. Task 1 owns it.
C4 is restated as a numbered first-match-wins list in which only the last outcome offers period options, removing the overlap between the scope case and the no-periods case.

C3 is split: task 1 (backend) proves one selector call for the question and none for a request carrying AskRequest.selection; task 2 proves only the exact continuation request body. The criterion says why a frontend test could not carry the claim.

Technical Approach gains a per-turn state model: a rerun names the turn it replaces, only that turn is pending, its previous successful response is retained throughout, and both a typed refusal and a thrown transport failure attach to that turn rather than to the panel.
Surface Impact is now a classified table with one row per required surface plus a reason on the Deferred and Unchanged-by-design rows.

Verify Plan now requires LLM_PROVIDER=bedrock, BEDROCK_MODEL_ID and AWS_REGION=ap-south-1 (decision 0027) alongside WAREHOUSE_PG_*, or the check reports itself BLOCKED rather than green - and states why, naming config.ts:178 and the mock provider's unconditional clarify.

HUMAN ROUND: the fields ship inside the deviation decision 0012 already records, and Surface Impact carries a Deferred row for the typed chat response DTO with a revisit trigger, to be logged with ./forge defer add.

The D-0006 claim is corrected rather than adopted: C10 now names backend/src/chat/chat.constants.ts as the ignored file this story touches, and states that chat.service.ts, contract/src/api.ts, ask-panel.tsx and use-ask.ts are not ignored - checked against .prettierignore rather than assumed.

rounds.question: The grill found that /api/chat documents its request body and error statuses but has no typed response DTO — its 201 carries only a description. Decision 0019 makes typed response DTOs mandatory for fresh routes; decision 0012 time-bounds the vendored deviation to the PoC. This story adds two new fields to that response. Pay the debt down now, or keep it inside the recorded deviation?
options: Keep the deviation, log a deferral (Recommended)
Type the chat response in this story
rounds.chosen: Keep the deviation, log a deferral (Recommended)
